checks_passed: Quotes in PREREG §1 match PAPER_EXTRACT.md word for word: 'random Gaussian distribution-initialized subspace', 'The input lengths are L = 104 for ILI and L = 96 for others.', 'The best parameters are selected based on the lowest validation loss.', 'We rerun all the experiments with codes provided by their official implementation.' Items still unverified against the PDF are marked [E], and the extract's reliability caveat is carried over.

Margins recomputed from the extract's Table 1: m_{192,PatchTST} = 0.460-0.423 = 0.037; m_{192,DLinear} = 0.434-0.423 = 0.011; m_{336,PatchTST} = 0.497-0.484 = 0.013; m_{336,DLinear} = 0.499-0.484 = 0.015. Best of the 8 baselines: 0.434 (DLinear) at H=192, 0.489 (FITS) at H=336, so m_192 = 0.011 and m_336 = 0.005. All correct.

Both D scales are defensible readings of 'random Gaussian distribution-initialized'. Neither is claimed to be the paper's (§5). N(0,1) is the torch.randn / nn.init.normal_ default. N(0,1/112) gives unit-norm columns, which is what D_constraint1 pulls towards (Constraint.py:14-17) and the scale of Initialization_D (InitializeD.py:50-67, SVD u columns). It is also exactly torch xavier_normal_ for a 112x112 matrix (std = sqrt(2/224)); the prereg does not mention this, and it adds support.

issues.issue: The FREEZE precondition checks too little to settle the margins. 'Eight cells' cannot establish which baseline is the best at H=192/336, because that needs every baseline cell in those rows. The fetch also inferred the column names, so a cell can be correct while sitting in the wrong column. Q2, Q2b and the anchor also use these numbers, but only Q3 labels get the fallback 'unverified' suffix.
issues.evidence: PREREG lines 13-17: 'the eight Table 1 cells used below (... TFPS, PatchTST, DLinear, and the best other baseline)'; fallback 'every Q3 label carries "margins per unverified extract"'. PAPER_EXTRACT.md:8: 'Table 1 cells were "reconstructed from garbled layout" by the fetch and column names were inferred'. The extract also hints at a garble: TSLANet and iTransformer are identical at H=96 (0.387/0.405) and at H=336 MSE (0.491). m_H (best baseline) drives Q2/Q2b EQUIVALENT and ', smaller than m_H' (§7). Paper values drive the anchor (§7).
issues.fix: Reword the precondition: 'the Table 1 column headers and the full ETTh1 MSE rows at H=192 and H=336 (all 9 models) are checked against the PDF and recorded in PAPER_EXTRACT.md; m_{H,B}, m_H and the anchor values are then recomputed'. Extend the fallback suffix to every Q2, Q2b, Q3 and anchor line that uses m_H, m_{H,B} or a paper value.

issues.issue: The 'm_{H,B} <= 0 means non-gating' rule is not carried into the Q3 rules. As written, a REVERSED/VANISHES label could still fire against a baseline that the paper itself does not claim to beat. That label would then read as a reversal of a claim the authors never made.
issues.evidence: §1 lines 29-30: 'If the checked m_{H,B} <= 0 for some (H, B), Q3 at that (H, B) becomes a non-gating descriptive comparison.' §7 rules 1-4 quantify over 'some B' / 'both B' in {patchtst, dlinear} with a Bonferroni split over two baselines. Nothing says what happens when one B is removed. The scenario is live: the r2 lens recalled DLinear ~0.481 at H=336, which would give m_{336,DLinear} < 0.
issues.fix: Add to §7: 'At a horizon where m_{H,B} <= 0, B is removed from rules 1-4 and from the horizon label and qualifiers. "Some B" and "both B" range over the remaining baselines. U uses one-sided (1 - 0.05/k) with k = the number of remaining baselines. d_{a,B} and its CI for a removed B are printed as descriptive. If no baseline remains, Q3 at H is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY.'

issues.issue: The input-length conflict can make Q3 harsher on TFPS than the paper's claim. If the paper's TFPS Table 1 values come from the appendix input-length search (best L in {96, 192, 336, 512}), then m_{H,B} includes any input-length advantage. A TFPS run fixed at L=96 is then expected to fall short of m_{H,B}, and VANISHES/SHRINKS ('claimed margin excluded') and ANCHOR DRIFT would partly reflect L, not the method. The suffix 'L=96' scopes the run but not the margin's provenance.
issues.evidence: PAPER_EXTRACT.md:19-21: 'we searched input lengths among 96, 192, 336, and 512, and report the best-performing configuration for each forecasting length' (described for TFPS) vs the caption 'L = 96 for others'; 'These two statements need reconciling against the PDF.' PREREG §1 line 21: 'not reconciled in the extract'. The FREEZE precondition (lines 13-17) does not include this check. The released scripts/etth1.sh uses seq_len 96 at :19/:75/:131/:188, so L=96 is a fair choice for the arms. The gap is only in how the margin is read.
issues.fix: Add to the FREEZE check: record the PDF context of the input-length sentence, i.e. whether it applies to TFPS's Table 1 numbers or to a separate study. If it applies, or if this cannot be settled, add to every negative Q3 label and to TFPS ANCHOR DRIFT: '— paper's TFPS values may come from an input-length search (L ∈ {96,192,336,512}); m_{H,B} may include an input-length gain not tested here'. No change to the arms.

summary: r3 tests TFPS as released, and the paper's claims are taken from exact extract quotes, with [E] marking what is unverified. Both D scales are defensible Gaussian readings, and neither is claimed to be the authors'. Baselines match the official PatchTST repo, and every deviation is stated. Margins are computed correctly from the extract. All §2 and §5 citations and sha256 values re-verify. All r2 fairness issues are fixed or partly fixed. Three major, non-blocking fixes are needed before FREEZE. (1) Widen the PDF check to full rows plus column headers, and apply the unverified suffix to Q2 and the anchor too. (2) Define how rules 1-4 behave once a baseline is non-gating, so no REVERSED fires against a claim the paper never made. (3) Settle the L-search sentence, or qualify negative labels with it. All three can be applied mechanically.
